ko.title: [물류 입문 #1] 아무도 눈에 띄지 않는 조 달러 규모 산업: 물류란 정확히 무엇인가

segments.src: > Logistics is the work of getting the right thing to the right place at the right time and cost — and in the U.S. it's roughly a $2.5 trillion-a-year industry that most people only notice when it fails.
segments.tr: > 물류는 올바른 물건을 올바른 장소에 올바른 시간과 비용으로 배송하는 일입니다. 미국에서 물류는 대략 연 2.5조 달러 규모의 산업이며, 대부분의 사람들은 실패할 때만 주목합니다.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Ask someone what logistics is and you'll usually hear "trucks."
segments.tr: 누군가에게 물류가 무엇인지 물어보면 보통 "트럭"이라는 답이 나옵니다.

segments.src: That's like saying finance is "ATMs."
segments.tr: 그것은 금융이 "ATM"이라고 말하는 것과 같습니다.

segments.src: The trade association CSCMP defines logistics management as the part of supply chain management that plans, implements, and controls the efficient flow and storage of goods, services, and related information — from the point of origin to the point of consumption, and back again.
segments.tr: 업계 단체 CSCMP는 물류 관리를 공급망 관리의 한 부분으로 정의합니다. 이는 원점에서 소비 지점까지, 그리고 다시 돌아오는 과정에서 물품, 서비스, 관련 정보의 효율적인 흐름과 저장을 계획, 구현, 제어합니다.

segments.src: Strip out the jargon and you get four verbs: **move, store, handle, inform.**
segments.tr: 전문 용어를 빼면 네 가지 동사가 나옵니다: **이동, 보관, 취급, 정보 전달.**

segments.src: Practitioners often summarize the goal as the **seven rights**: the right product, in the right quantity, in the right condition, at the right place, at the right time, to the right customer, at the right cost.
segments.tr: 전문가들은 목표를 **일곱 가지 올바름**으로 정리합니다: 올바른 제품, 올바른 수량, 올바른 상태, 올바른 장소, 올바른 시간, 올바른 고객, 올바른 비용.

segments.src: Notice that six of the seven are about *service* and only one is about *price*.
segments.tr: 일곱 가지 중 여섯 가지는 *서비스*에 관한 것이고 하나만 *가격*에 관한 것임을 주목하세요.

segments.src: That tension is the entire discipline.
segments.tr: 그 긴장 관계가 바로 이 분야 전체입니다.

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: logistics doesn't change what a product *is*.
segments.tr: 사람들을 놀라게 하는 부분은 이것입니다: 물류는 제품이 *무엇인지*는 바꾸지 않습니다.

segments.src: A pair of running shoes sitting in a warehouse in Ohio is chemically identical to the same pair on your doorstep in Denver.
segments.tr: 오하이오 창고에 있는 한 켤레의 러닝화와 덴버의 당신의 현관에 있는 같은 켤레는 화학적으로 동일합니다.

segments.src: What logistics creates is **place utility** (value from being where you need it) and **time utility** (value from being there when you need it).
segments.tr: 물류가 만드는 것은 **위치 효용성**(필요한 곳에 있음으로써 생기는 가치)과 **시간 효용성**(필요한 때에 있음으로써 생기는 가치)입니다.

segments.src: An umbrella in a warehouse is inventory.
segments.tr: 창고에 있는 우산은 재고입니다.

segments.src: An umbrella in a store lobby during a downpour is a sale.
segments.tr: 폭우 중 상점 로비의 우산은 판매입니다.

segments.src: **So how is this different from supply chain management?** Think of nested boxes.
segments.tr: **그럼 공급망 관리와는 어떻게 다를까요?** 중첩된 상자를 생각해보세요.

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM) is the bigger box — it covers sourcing raw materials, negotiating with suppliers, planning production, forecasting demand, and coordinating everyone from the cotton farmer to the cashier.
segments.tr: 공급망 관리(SCM)는 더 큰 상자입니다. 원재료 조달, 공급업체와의 협상, 생산 계획, 수요 예측, 그리고 면화 농부부터 계산원까지 모든 사람을 조율하는 것을 포함합니다.

segments.src: Logistics is the box inside it that handles physical flow and storage.
segments.tr: 물류는 그 안의 상자로, 물리적 흐름과 저장을 담당합니다.

segments.src: A useful shorthand:
segments.tr: 유용한 요약:

segments.src: - **SCM asks:** who should make this, where, in what quantity, and on what terms?
segments.tr: - **SCM이 묻는 것:** 누가 이것을 만들어야 하며, 어디서, 어떤 수량으로, 어떤 조건으로?

segments.src: - **Logistics asks:** given those decisions, how does it physically get there, how fast, and at what cost?
segments.tr: - **물류가 묻는 것:** 그 결정들을 고려할 때, 어떻게 물리적으로 도착하며, 얼마나 빠르게, 어떤 비용으로?

segments.src: You can't do good SCM without logistics, but logistics alone won't save you from a bad sourcing decision.
segments.tr: 물류 없이는 좋은 SCM을 할 수 없지만, 물류만으로는 나쁜 조달 결정으로부터 당신을 구할 수 없습니다.

segments.src: If your supplier is 8,000 miles away and your product has a six-week shelf life, no amount of clever routing fixes that.
segments.tr: 만약 당신의 공급업체가 8,000마일 떨어져 있고 제품의 유통기한이 6주라면, 아무리 영리한 경로 계획도 그것을 해결할 수 없습니다.

segments.src: The other thing to know upfront: logistics is a **trade-off machine**, not an optimization with one answer.
segments.tr: 또 알아야 할 중요한 점: 물류는 **트레이드오프 기계**이지, 하나의 정답을 가진 최적화가 아닙니다.

segments.src: Air freight is fast and expensive; ocean is cheap and slow.
segments.tr: 항공 운송은 빠르고 비싸고; 해상 운송은 싸고 느립니다.

segments.src: Holding lots of inventory means you never stock out, but the industry rule of thumb is that carrying inventory costs roughly 20–25% of its value per year in capital, warehousing, insurance, and obsolescence.
segments.tr: 많은 재고를 보유하면 품절될 일이 없지만, 업계 경험칙에 따르면 재고 유지 비용은 자본, 창고, 보험, 노후화를 포함하여 연간 가치의 약 20-25%입니다.

segments.src: Five regional warehouses shorten delivery times but multiply fixed costs.
segments.tr: 5개의 지역 창고는 배송 시간을 단축하지만 고정 비용을 배로 늘립니다.

segments.src: Every logistics decision is somebody choosing a point on a curve — usually the curve between **cost and speed**, or between **cost and reliability**.
segments.tr: 모든 물류 결정은 누군가가 곡선 위의 한 점을 선택하는 것입니다 — 보통 **비용과 속도** 사이의 곡선, 또는 **비용과 신뢰성** 사이의 곡선입니다.

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: You order running shoes for $89 on a Sunday night from your couch in Denver.
segments.tr: 당신은 일요일 밤에 덴버의 소파에서 $89의 러닝화를 주문합니다.

segments.src: Free two-day shipping.
segments.tr: 무료 2일 배송.

segments.src: Here's the invisible machine that runs before Tuesday.
segments.tr: 다음은 화요일 전에 작동하는 보이지 않는 기계입니다.

segments.src: The moment you click, an inventory system decides *which* of several U.S.
segments.tr: 클릭하는 순간, 재고 시스템이 여러 미국

segments.src: fulfillment centers should ship — not necessarily the closest one, but the one that balances distance, stock levels, and how many other Denver-bound orders it can consolidate into the same truck.
segments.tr: 이행 센터 중 어느 것이 배송할지 결정합니다 — 반드시 가장 가까운 것이 아니라, 거리, 재고 수준, 그리고 같은 트럭으로 통합할 수 있는 다른 덴버행 주문의 수 사이의 균형을 맞추는 것입니다.

segments.src: A worker (or increasingly, a robotic shelf-mover) picks your box, and it gets sorted onto a line-haul truck.
segments.tr: 작업자(또는 점점 더 많아지는 로봇 선반 이동기)가 당신의 상자를 선택하고, 그것이 장거리 운송 트럭으로 분류됩니다.

segments.src: That truck may run to a sorting hub — the two most famous in the country are UPS's Worldport in Louisville, Kentucky, and FedEx's superhub in Memphis, Tennessee, both of which exist because they sit near the population-weighted center of the U.S.
segments.tr: 그 트럭은 분류 허브로 갈 수 있습니다 — 국가에서 가장 유명한 두 곳은 켄터키주 루이빌의 UPS 월드포트와 테네시주 멤피스의 페덱스 슈퍼허브이며, 둘 다 미국의 인구 가중 중심 근처에 있기 때문에 존재합니다.

segments.src: and let packages from everywhere meet, re-sort overnight, and fly back out before dawn.
segments.tr: 그리고 모든 곳에서 온 패키지들이 만나고, 밤새 재분류되며, 새벽 전에 다시 날아갑니다.

segments.src: From there your box moves to a local delivery station, gets loaded onto a van with 150 other stops, and a route algorithm decides the driver's sequence.
segments.tr: 거기서부터 당신의 상자는 지역 배송 센터로 이동하고, 다른 150개의 정거장과 함께 밴에 실려 가며, 경로 알고리즘이 운전자의 순서를 결정합니다.

segments.src: That final leg — the delivery station to your door — is called the **last mile**, and it's routinely the single most expensive segment of the whole journey.
segments.tr: 그 마지막 구간 — 배송 센터에서 당신의 집까지 — 은 **마지막 마일**이라고 불리며, 전체 여정에서 일관되게 가장 비싼 구간입니다.

segments.src: One truck crossing Nebraska carries thousands of packages at once; one van in a Denver neighborhood carries a few hundred and burns an hour in traffic.
segments.tr: 네브래스카를 횡단하는 하나의 트럭은 한 번에 수천 개의 패키지를 운반합니다; 덴버 동네의 한 밴은 수백 개를 운반하고 교통 체증으로 한 시간을 낭비합니다.

segments.src: Trucking is the largest single line item in U.S.
segments.tr: 트럭 운송은 미국

segments.src: logistics spending, and last-mile delivery is why.
segments.tr: 물류 지출에서 가장 큰 단일 항목이며, 마지막 마일 배송이 그 이유입니다.

segments.src: "Free shipping" is, of course, not free.
segments.tr: "무료 배송"은 물론 무료가 아닙니다.

segments.src: It's priced into the $89, subsidized by your membership fee, or absorbed as a customer-acquisition cost.
segments.tr: 그것은 $89에 포함된 가격이거나, 당신의 멤버십 요금으로 보조되거나, 고객 획득 비용으로 흡수됩니다.

segments.src: Somebody paid for the van.
segments.tr: 누군가는 그 밴의 비용을 지불했습니다.

segments.src: Now zoom out.
segments.tr: 이제 전체적으로 봅시다.

segments.src: Recent CSCMP *State of Logistics* reports put total U.S.
segments.tr: 최근 CSCMP *물류 현황* 보고서는 총 미국

segments.src: business logistics costs at roughly **$2.5 trillion, or about 8–9% of GDP**.
segments.tr: 비즈니스 물류 비용을 대략 **$2.5조 달러, 또는 GDP의 약 8-9%**로 추정합니다.

segments.src: That's the scale of the industry that made your Tuesday delivery unremarkable.
segments.tr: 이것이 당신의 화요일 배송을 평범하게 만든 산업의 규모입니다.

segments.src: And it's changing fast.
segments.tr: 그리고 그것은 빠르게 변하고 있습니다.

segments.src: Four trends worth knowing:
segments.tr: 알아둘 가치가 있는 네 가지 추세:

segments.src: 1. **E-commerce reshaped the network.** Retail logistics used to mean moving pallets to a few hundred stores. Now it means moving single boxes to millions of homes — a completely different cost structure, which is why warehouse space near cities got so valuable.
segments.tr: 1. **전자상거래가 네트워크를 재편성했습니다.** 소매 물류는 팔레트를 수백 개의 상점으로 이동하는 것을 의미했습니다. 이제는 단일 상자를 수백만 개의 가정으로 이동하는 것을 의미합니다 — 완전히 다른 비용 구조로, 도시 근처의 창고 공간이 매우 가치 있게 된 이유입니다.

segments.src: 2. **Automation is filling warehouses**, driven by both labor shortages and volume — robotic picking, automated sortation, and warehouse management software.
segments.tr: 2. **자동화가 창고를 채우고 있으며**, 노동력 부족과 물량 모두에 의해 주도됩니다 — 로봇 피킹, 자동화된 분류, 창고 관리 소프트웨어.

segments.src: 3. **Resilience is now a board-level word.** The 2020–2022 disruptions — port congestion, the Suez blockage, chip shortages — taught companies that the cheapest supply chain and the most reliable one are rarely the same. Hence "nearshoring," dual sourcing, and holding a bit more safety stock than pure efficiency would suggest.
segments.tr: 3. **탄력성은 이제 이사회 수준의 단어입니다.** 2020-2022년의 중단 — 항만 혼잡, 수에즈 봉쇄, 칩 부족 — 은 기업들에게 가장 싼 공급망과 가장 신뢰할 수 있는 공급망이 거의 같지 않다는 것을 가르쳤습니다. 따라서 "근처 아웃소싱," 이중 조달, 그리고 순수 효율성이 제시하는 것보다 조금 더 많은 안전 재고를 보유합니다.

segments.src: 4. **Visibility is the new battleground.** Knowing exactly where a shipment is, and predicting when it will actually arrive, is often worth more than shaving a few cents off the freight rate.
segments.tr: 4. **가시성이 새로운 전쟁터입니다.** 배송물이 정확히 어디에 있는지 알고 실제로 도착할 때를 예측하는 것은 종종 운임에서 몇 센트를 깎는 것보다 더 가치가 있습니다.

segments.src: A last practical concept: when comparing two suppliers, the sticker price is the wrong number.
segments.tr: 마지막 실용적인 개념: 두 공급업체를 비교할 때, 스티커 가격은 잘못된 숫자입니다.

segments.src: What matters is **landed cost**:
segments.tr: 중요한 것은 **착지 비용**입니다:

segments.src: Landed cost = unit price + freight + duties/tariffs + insurance + handling
segments.tr: Landed cost = unit price + freight + duties/tariffs + insurance + handling

segments.src: A part that's 15% cheaper from overseas can easily be more expensive once it lands.
segments.tr: 해외에서 15% 더 싼 부품은 착지하면 쉽게 더 비싸질 수 있습니다.

segments.src: That single line is why logistics belongs in strategy meetings and not just in the loading dock.
segments.tr: 그 한 줄이 물류가 전략 회의에 속하고 단지 로딩 도크에만 속하지 않는 이유입니다.

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 3줄 정리

segments.src: 1. Logistics is the move-store-handle-inform work that creates **place and time utility** — it doesn't change the product, it changes where and when it's available.
segments.tr: 1. 물류는 **위치 및 시간 효용성**을 창출하는 이동-보관-취급-정보 작업입니다 — 제품을 바꾸지 않고, 제품이 어디서 언제 사용 가능한지를 바꿉니다.

segments.src: 2. Logistics is a **subset of supply chain management**: SCM decides who makes what, where, and how much; logistics executes the physical flow and storage.
segments.tr: 2. 물류는 **공급망 관리의 부분집합**입니다: SCM은 누가 무엇을, 어디서, 얼마나 많이 만들 것인지를 결정합니다; 물류는 물리적 흐름과 저장을 실행합니다.

segments.src: 3. Every logistics decision is a **trade-off** among cost, speed, and reliability — and the honest number to compare is landed cost, not sticker price.
segments.tr: 3. 모든 물류 결정은 비용, 속도, 신뢰성 간의 **트레이드오프**입니다 — 그리고 비교할 정직한 숫자는 착지 비용이지, 스티커 가격이 아닙니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.src: **1.** Which statement best describes the relationship between logistics and supply chain management?
segments.tr: **1.** 물류와 공급망 관리 간의 관계를 가장 잘 설명하는 진술은 무엇입니까?

segments.src: - (A) They are two words for exactly the same thing.
segments.tr: - (A) 그들은 정확히 같은 것에 대한 두 단어입니다.

segments.src: - (B) Logistics is a component of supply chain management, focused on physical flow and storage.
segments.tr: - (B) 물류는 공급망 관리의 구성요소이며, 물리적 흐름과 저장에 중점을 둡니다.

segments.src: - (C) Supply chain management is a component of logistics.
segments.tr: - (C) 공급망 관리는 물류의 구성요소입니다.

segments.src: - (D) Logistics covers strategy; supply chain management covers trucks.
segments.tr: - (D) 물류는 전략을 다루고; 공급망 관리는 트럭을 다룹니다.

segments.src: **2.** In a typical parcel delivery, which leg is usually the most expensive per package?
segments.tr: **2.** 일반적인 소포 배송에서, 일반적으로 패키지당 가장 비싼 구간은 어느 것입니까?

segments.src: - (A) The ocean crossing
segments.tr: - (A) 해양 횡단

segments.src: - (B) The long-haul truck between hubs
segments.tr: - (B) 허브 간 장거리 트럭

segments.src: - (C) The last mile, from local station to the customer's door
segments.tr: - (C) 마지막 마일, 지역 센터에서 고객의 현관까지

segments.src: - (D) The initial pick-and-pack in the warehouse
segments.tr: - (D) 창고의 초기 피킹 및 패킹

segments.src: **3.** (O/X) Because logistics doesn't physically alter a product, it doesn't add real economic value.

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Logistics** — Planning and controlling the efficient flow and storage of goods, services, and related information from origin to consumption, including returns.
segments.tr: - **물류** — 원점에서 소비까지 물품, 서비스, 관련 정보의 효율적인 흐름과 저장을 계획하고 제어하며, 반품을 포함합니다.

segments.src: - **Supply Chain Management (SCM)** — The broader coordination of sourcing, production, planning, and distribution across all partners from raw material to end customer; logistics sits inside it.
segments.tr: - **공급망 관리(SCM)** — 원재료에서 최종 고객까지 모든 파트너 간 조달, 생산, 계획, 유통의 광범위한 조율; 물류는 그 안에 있습니다.

segments.src: - **Last mile** — The final delivery leg from a local facility to the customer's door; typically the most expensive segment per package.
segments.tr: - **마지막 마일** — 지역 시설에서 고객의 현관까지의 최종 배송 구간; 일반적으로 패키지당 가장 비싼 구간입니다.

segments.src: - **Lead time** — Total elapsed time from placing an order to receiving it; the number customers actually feel.
segments.tr: - **리드 타임** — 주문 배치에서 수령까지의 총 경과 시간; 고객이 실제로 느끼는 숫자입니다.

segments.src: - **Landed cost** — The all-in cost of getting a purchased item to your door: unit price plus freight, duties, insurance, and handling.
segments.tr: - **착지 비용** — 구매한 항목을 당신의 현관까지 가져가는 전체 비용: 단위 가격 플러스 운임, 관세, 보험, 취급.

segments.src: - **3PL (third-party logistics)** — An outside company hired to run warehousing, transportation, or fulfillment on your behalf instead of doing it in-house.
segments.tr: - **3PL(제3자 물류)** — 사내에서 하는 대신 당신을 대신하여 창고, 운송, 이행을 실행하도록 고용된 외부 회사입니다.

segments.src: Logistics is the physical-flow-and-storage piece nested inside the wider SCM function, which also covers sourcing, demand planning, and supplier strategy.
segments.tr: 물류는 물리적 흐름과 저장을 담당하는 부분으로, 조달, 수요 계획, 공급업체 전략도 다루는 더 광범위한 SCM 기능 내에 포함되어 있습니다.

segments.src: Long-haul legs spread their cost across thousands of packages; a delivery van covers far fewer stops per hour, so the last mile carries a disproportionate share of total delivery cost.

zh.title: [物流101 #1] 万亿美元的隐形工作：物流究竟是什么

segments.src: > Logistics is the work of getting the right thing to the right place at the right time and cost — and in the U.S. it's roughly a $2.5 trillion-a-year industry that most people only notice when it fails.
segments.tr: > 物流是指在适当的时间和成本下，将正确的商品送到正确地点的工作——在美国，这大约是一个价值2.5万亿美元的年产业，大多数人只在它失败时才会注意到它。

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Ask someone what logistics is and you'll usually hear "trucks."
segments.tr: 问别人什么是物流，你通常会听到"卡车"。

segments.src: That's like saying finance is "ATMs."
segments.tr: 这就像说金融就是"自动取款机"。

segments.src: The trade association CSCMP defines logistics management as the part of supply chain management that plans, implements, and controls the efficient flow and storage of goods, services, and related information — from the point of origin to the point of consumption, and back again.
segments.tr: 贸易协会CSCMP将物流管理定义为供应链管理的一部分，它规划、实施和控制商品、服务和相关信息的高效流动和储存——从原点到消费点，以及回程。

segments.src: Strip out the jargon and you get four verbs: **move, store, handle, inform.**
segments.tr: 删除行话，你会得到四个动词：**移动、储存、处理、通知。**

segments.src: Practitioners often summarize the goal as the **seven rights**: the right product, in the right quantity, in the right condition, at the right place, at the right time, to the right customer, at the right cost.
segments.tr: 从业者通常将目标总结为**七个正确**：正确的产品、正确的数量、正确的状况、正确的地点、正确的时间、正确的客户、正确的成本。

segments.src: Notice that six of the seven are about *service* and only one is about *price*.
segments.tr: 注意，七个中有六个是关于*服务*的，只有一个是关于*价格*的。

segments.src: That tension is the entire discipline.
segments.tr: 这种张力就是整个学科。

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: logistics doesn't change what a product *is*.
segments.tr: 这是令人惊讶的部分：物流不会改变产品的*本质*。

segments.src: A pair of running shoes sitting in a warehouse in Ohio is chemically identical to the same pair on your doorstep in Denver.
segments.tr: 放在俄亥俄州仓库里的一双跑鞋在化学上与你丹佛门前的同一双鞋完全相同。

segments.src: What logistics creates is **place utility** (value from being where you need it) and **time utility** (value from being there when you need it).
segments.tr: 物流创造的是**地点效用**（从在你需要的地点获得的价值）和**时间效用**（从在你需要的时候在那里获得的价值）。

segments.src: An umbrella in a warehouse is inventory.
segments.tr: 仓库里的伞是库存。

segments.src: An umbrella in a store lobby during a downpour is a sale.
segments.tr: 大雨中商店大厅里的伞是一笔销售。

segments.src: **So how is this different from supply chain management?** Think of nested boxes.
segments.tr: **那么这与供应链管理有什么不同呢？**想象嵌套的盒子。

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM) is the bigger box — it covers sourcing raw materials, negotiating with suppliers, planning production, forecasting demand, and coordinating everyone from the cotton farmer to the cashier.
segments.tr: 供应链管理（SCM）是更大的盒子——它涵盖采购原材料、与供应商谈判、计划生产、预测需求，以及协调从棉花农民到收银员的所有人员。

segments.src: Logistics is the box inside it that handles physical flow and storage.
segments.tr: 物流是其中处理物理流动和储存的盒子。

segments.src: A useful shorthand:
segments.tr: 一个有用的简写：

segments.src: - **SCM asks:** who should make this, where, in what quantity, and on what terms?
segments.tr: - **SCM问的是：**谁应该做这个，在哪里，数量多少，条件是什么？

segments.src: - **Logistics asks:** given those decisions, how does it physically get there, how fast, and at what cost?
segments.tr: - **物流问的是：**鉴于这些决定，它如何实际到达那里，速度有多快，成本是多少？

segments.src: You can't do good SCM without logistics, but logistics alone won't save you from a bad sourcing decision.
segments.tr: 没有物流，你无法做好SCM，但仅靠物流无法挽救你的坏采购决定。

segments.src: If your supplier is 8,000 miles away and your product has a six-week shelf life, no amount of clever routing fixes that.
segments.tr: 如果你的供应商离你8000英里，而你的产品保质期为六周，再聪明的路线也救不了。

segments.src: The other thing to know upfront: logistics is a **trade-off machine**, not an optimization with one answer.
segments.tr: 另一件要预先知道的事情是：物流是一台**权衡机器**，而不是有一个答案的优化。

segments.src: Air freight is fast and expensive; ocean is cheap and slow.
segments.tr: 空运快速且昂贵；海运便宜且缓慢。

segments.src: Holding lots of inventory means you never stock out, but the industry rule of thumb is that carrying inventory costs roughly 20–25% of its value per year in capital, warehousing, insurance, and obsolescence.
segments.tr: 持有大量库存意味着你永远不会缺货，但行业经验法则是，持有库存每年的成本大约是其价值的20-25%，包括资本、仓储、保险和报废。

segments.src: Five regional warehouses shorten delivery times but multiply fixed costs.
segments.tr: 五个地区仓库缩短了交付时间，但增加了固定成本。

segments.src: Every logistics decision is somebody choosing a point on a curve — usually the curve between **cost and speed**, or between **cost and reliability**.
segments.tr: 每个物流决定都是某人在曲线上选择一个点——通常是**成本和速度**之间的曲线，或**成本和可靠性**之间的曲线。

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## 일상 속에서

segments.src: You order running shoes for $89 on a Sunday night from your couch in Denver.
segments.tr: 你在周日晚上从丹佛的沙发上订购了一双89美元的跑鞋。

segments.src: Free two-day shipping.
segments.tr: 免费两天配送。

segments.src: Here's the invisible machine that runs before Tuesday.
segments.tr: 这是在星期二之前运行的看不见的机器。

segments.src: The moment you click, an inventory system decides *which* of several U.S.
segments.tr: 你点击的瞬间，库存系统决定了来自几家美国

segments.src: fulfillment centers should ship — not necessarily the closest one, but the one that balances distance, stock levels, and how many other Denver-bound orders it can consolidate into the same truck.
segments.tr: 履行中心中*哪一家*应该配送——不一定是最近的一家，而是平衡距离、库存水平，以及可以整合到同一辆卡车中的其他丹佛订单数量的那一家。

segments.src: A worker (or increasingly, a robotic shelf-mover) picks your box, and it gets sorted onto a line-haul truck.
segments.tr: 一个工人（或越来越多地，一个机器人架子移动器）挑选你的盒子，它被分类到干线卡车上。

segments.src: That truck may run to a sorting hub — the two most famous in the country are UPS's Worldport in Louisville, Kentucky, and FedEx's superhub in Memphis, Tennessee, both of which exist because they sit near the population-weighted center of the U.S.
segments.tr: 那辆卡车可能会驶向一个分类枢纽——该国最著名的两个是位于肯塔基州路易维尔的UPS Worldport和位于田纳西州孟菲斯的FedEx超级枢纽，它们存在是因为它们位于美国人口加权中心附近。

segments.src: and let packages from everywhere meet, re-sort overnight, and fly back out before dawn.
segments.tr: 并让来自各地的包裹相遇、在一夜之间重新分类，然后在黎明前飞出去。

segments.src: From there your box moves to a local delivery station, gets loaded onto a van with 150 other stops, and a route algorithm decides the driver's sequence.
segments.tr: 从那里，你的盒子移动到本地配送站，与150个其他停靠点一起装上一辆货车，路线算法决定了司机的顺序。

segments.src: That final leg — the delivery station to your door — is called the **last mile**, and it's routinely the single most expensive segment of the whole journey.
segments.tr: 从配送站到你家门口的最后一段——被称为**最后一公里**，它通常是整个旅程中单一的最昂贵的部分。

segments.src: One truck crossing Nebraska carries thousands of packages at once; one van in a Denver neighborhood carries a few hundred and burns an hour in traffic.
segments.tr: 一辆穿过内布拉斯加州的卡车一次运载数千个包裹；丹佛社区的一辆面包车运载几百个包裹，并在交通中消耗一个小时。

segments.src: Trucking is the largest single line item in U.S.
segments.tr: 卡车运输是美国最大的单一项目。

segments.src: logistics spending, and last-mile delivery is why.
segments.tr: 物流支出中，最后一公里配送就是原因。

segments.src: "Free shipping" is, of course, not free.
segments.tr: "免费配送"当然不是免费的。

segments.src: It's priced into the $89, subsidized by your membership fee, or absorbed as a customer-acquisition cost.
segments.tr: 它被计入89美元，由你的会员费补贴，或作为客户获取成本被吸收。

segments.src: Somebody paid for the van.
segments.tr: 有人为那辆货车付钱。

segments.src: Now zoom out.
segments.tr: 现在缩小范围。

segments.src: Recent CSCMP *State of Logistics* reports put total U.S.
segments.tr: 最近的CSCMP《物流状况》报告将美国总体

segments.src: business logistics costs at roughly **$2.5 trillion, or about 8–9% of GDP**.
segments.tr: 业务物流成本定为大约**2.5万亿美元，或约占GDP的8-9%**。

segments.src: That's the scale of the industry that made your Tuesday delivery unremarkable.
segments.tr: 这就是使你的星期二配送不足为奇的行业规模。

segments.src: And it's changing fast.
segments.tr: 它正在快速变化。

segments.src: Four trends worth knowing:
segments.tr: 四个值得了解的趋势：

segments.src: 1. **E-commerce reshaped the network.** Retail logistics used to mean moving pallets to a few hundred stores. Now it means moving single boxes to millions of homes — a completely different cost structure, which is why warehouse space near cities got so valuable.
segments.tr: 1. **电子商务改变了网络。**零售物流过去意味着将托盘运送到几百家商店。现在意味着将单个盒子运送到数百万个家庭——一个完全不同的成本结构，这就是为什么城市附近的仓库空间变得如此宝贵。

segments.src: 2. **Automation is filling warehouses**, driven by both labor shortages and volume — robotic picking, automated sortation, and warehouse management software.
segments.tr: 2. **自动化正在填充仓库**，由劳动力短缺和数量驱动——机器人选货、自动分类和仓库管理软件。

segments.src: 3. **Resilience is now a board-level word.** The 2020–2022 disruptions — port congestion, the Suez blockage, chip shortages — taught companies that the cheapest supply chain and the most reliable one are rarely the same. Hence "nearshoring," dual sourcing, and holding a bit more safety stock than pure efficiency would suggest.
segments.tr: 3. **抗灾力现在是董事会级的词。**2020-2022年的中断——港口拥堵、苏伊士运河封锁、芯片短缺——教会了公司，最便宜的供应链和最可靠的供应链很少相同。因此"近岸外包"、双源和持有比纯效率建议的更多安全库存。

segments.src: 4. **Visibility is the new battleground.** Knowing exactly where a shipment is, and predicting when it will actually arrive, is often worth more than shaving a few cents off the freight rate.
segments.tr: 4. **可见性是新的战场。**准确知道货物在哪里，并预测它何时会实际到达，通常比降低运费几美分更有价值。

segments.src: A last practical concept: when comparing two suppliers, the sticker price is the wrong number.
segments.tr: 最后一个实际概念：在比较两个供应商时，标价是错误的数字。

segments.src: What matters is **landed cost**:
segments.tr: 重要的是**到岸成本**：

segments.src: Landed cost = unit price + freight + duties/tariffs + insurance + handling
segments.tr: Landed cost = unit price + freight + duties/tariffs + insurance + handling

segments.src: A part that's 15% cheaper from overseas can easily be more expensive once it lands.
segments.tr: 从海外便宜15%的零件到岸后很容易变得更贵。

segments.src: That single line is why logistics belongs in strategy meetings and not just in the loading dock.
segments.tr: 这一条线就是为什么物流应该出现在战略会议中，而不仅仅是在码头上。

segments.src: ## 3줄 정리
segments.tr: ## 3줄 정리

segments.src: 1. Logistics is the move-store-handle-inform work that creates **place and time utility** — it doesn't change the product, it changes where and when it's available.
segments.tr: 1. 物流是创造**地点和时间效用**的移动-储存-处理-通知工作——它不改变产品，而是改变它在哪里和何时可用。

segments.src: 2. Logistics is a **subset of supply chain management**: SCM decides who makes what, where, and how much; logistics executes the physical flow and storage.
segments.tr: 2. 物流是**供应链管理的子集**：SCM决定谁做什么、在哪里做、做多少；物流执行物理流动和储存。

segments.src: 3. Every logistics decision is a **trade-off** among cost, speed, and reliability — and the honest number to compare is landed cost, not sticker price.
segments.tr: 3. 每个物流决定都是在成本、速度和可靠性之间的**权衡**——要比较的诚实数字是到岸成本，而不是标价。

segments.src: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.tr: **1.** 哪个陈述最好地描述了物流和供应链管理之间的关系？

segments.tr: - (A) 它们是完全相同事物的两个词。

segments.tr: - (B) 物流是供应链管理的一个组成部分，专注于物理流动和储存。

segments.src: - (C) Supply chain management is a component of logistics.
segments.tr: - (C) 供应链管理是物流的一个组成部分。

segments.tr: - (D) 物流涵盖战略；供应链管理涵盖卡车。

segments.src: **2.** In a typical parcel delivery, which leg is usually the most expensive per package?
segments.tr: **2.** 在典型的包裹配送中，哪一段通常对每个包裹来说成本最高？

segments.tr: - (A) 海洋穿越

segments.tr: **3.** (O/X) 因为物流不会物理上改变产品，它不会增加真实的经济价值。

segments.src: ## 📚 오늘의 용어
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Logistics** — Planning and controlling the efficient flow and storage of goods, services, and related information from origin to consumption, including returns.
segments.tr: - **物流** — 规划和控制商品、服务和相关信息从原产地到消费的高效流动和储存，包括退货。

segments.src: - **Supply Chain Management (SCM)** — The broader coordination of sourcing, production, planning, and distribution across all partners from raw material to end customer; logistics sits inside it.
segments.tr: - **供应链管理（SCM）** — 从原材料到最终客户的所有合作伙伴之间采购、生产、规划和分配的更广泛协调；物流在其中。

segments.src: - **Last mile** — The final delivery leg from a local facility to the customer's door; typically the most expensive segment per package.
segments.tr: - **最后一公里** — 从本地设施到客户门口的最终配送段；通常是每个包裹最昂贵的部分。

segments.src: - **Lead time** — Total elapsed time from placing an order to receiving it; the number customers actually feel.
segments.tr: - **交付期** — 从下单到收到的总用时；客户实际感受到的时间。

segments.src: - **Landed cost** — The all-in cost of getting a purchased item to your door: unit price plus freight, duties, insurance, and handling.
segments.tr: - **到岸成本** — 将购买的物品送到你门口的总成本：单位价格加运费、关税、保险和处理费用。

segments.src: - **3PL (third-party logistics)** — An outside company hired to run warehousing, transportation, or fulfillment on your behalf instead of doing it in-house.
segments.tr: - **第三方物流（3PL）** — 被雇来代表你运营仓储、运输或履行，而不是内部进行的外部公司。

segments.src: Logistics is the physical-flow-and-storage piece nested inside the wider SCM function, which also covers sourcing, demand planning, and supplier strategy.
segments.tr: 物流是嵌套在更广泛的SCM功能中的物理流动和储存部分，它还涵盖采购、需求规划和供应商战略。

hi.title: [लॉजिस्टिक्स 101 #1] ट्रिलियन-डॉलर की नौकरी जो कोई नहीं देखता: लॉजिस्टिक्स वास्तव में क्या है

segments.src: > Logistics is the work of getting the right thing to the right place at the right time and cost — and in the U.S. it's roughly a $2.5 trillion-a-year industry that most people only notice when it fails.
segments.tr: > लॉजिस्टिक्स सही चीज को सही जगह पर सही समय और सही लागत पर पहुंचाने का काम है — और यू.एस. में यह लगभग $2.5 ट्रिलियन प्रति वर्ष का उद्योग है जिसे ज्यादातर लोग केवल तब नोटिस करते हैं जब यह विफल हो जाता है।

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Ask someone what logistics is and you'll usually hear "trucks."
segments.tr: किसी से पूछें कि लॉजिस्टिक्स क्या है और आप आमतौर पर "ट्रक" सुनेंगे।

segments.src: That's like saying finance is "ATMs."
segments.tr: यह कहने जैसा है कि वित्त "ATM" है।

segments.src: The trade association CSCMP defines logistics management as the part of supply chain management that plans, implements, and controls the efficient flow and storage of goods, services, and related information — from the point of origin to the point of consumption, and back again.
segments.tr: व्यापार संघ CSCMP लॉजिस्टिक्स प्रबंधन को आपूर्ति श्रृंखला प्रबंधन के उस हिस्से के रूप में परिभाषित करता है जो वस्तुओं, सेवाओं और संबंधित जानकारी के कुशल प्रवाह और भंडारण की योजना बनाता है, लागू करता है और नियंत्रण करता है — उत्पत्ति के बिंदु से खपत के बिंदु तक, और फिर से वापस।

segments.src: Strip out the jargon and you get four verbs: **move, store, handle, inform.**
segments.tr: तकनीकी शब्दावली को हटाएं और आपको चार क्रियाएं मिलती हैं: **स्थानांतरित करें, संग्रहीत करें, संभालें, सूचित करें।**

segments.src: Practitioners often summarize the goal as the **seven rights**: the right product, in the right quantity, in the right condition, at the right place, at the right time, to the right customer, at the right cost.
segments.tr: चिकित्सक अक्सर लक्ष्य को **सात अधिकार** के रूप में सारांशित करते हैं: सही उत्पाद, सही मात्रा में, सही स्थिति में, सही जगह पर, सही समय पर, सही ग्राहक को, सही लागत पर।

segments.src: Notice that six of the seven are about *service* and only one is about *price*.
segments.tr: ध्यान दें कि सात में से छह *सेवा* के बारे में हैं और केवल एक *मूल्य* के बारे में है।

segments.src: That tension is the entire discipline.
segments.tr: वह तनाव पूरी अनुशासन है।

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: logistics doesn't change what a product *is*.
segments.tr: यहाँ वह हिस्सा है जो लोगों को आश्चर्यचकित करता है: लॉजिस्टिक्स यह नहीं बदलता कि कोई उत्पाद *क्या* है।

segments.src: A pair of running shoes sitting in a warehouse in Ohio is chemically identical to the same pair on your doorstep in Denver.
segments.tr: ओहियो के एक गोदाम में बैठे दौड़ने के जूते की एक जोड़ी डेनवर में आपकी चौखट पर समान जोड़ी के समान रासायनिक रूप से समान है।

segments.src: What logistics creates is **place utility** (value from being where you need it) and **time utility** (value from being there when you need it).
segments.tr: लॉजिस्टिक्स जो बनाता है वह है **स्थान उपयोगिता** (जहां आपको इसकी आवश्यकता है वहां होने से मूल्य) और **समय उपयोगिता** (जहां आपको इसकी आवश्यकता है वहां होने से मूल्य)।

segments.src: An umbrella in a warehouse is inventory.
segments.tr: गोदाम में एक छत्र स्टॉक है।

segments.src: An umbrella in a store lobby during a downpour is a sale.
segments.tr: बारिश के समय स्टोर लॉबी में एक छत्र एक बिक्री है।

segments.src: **So how is this different from supply chain management?** Think of nested boxes.
segments.tr: **तो यह आपूर्ति श्रृंखला प्रबंधन से कैसे अलग है?** नेस्टेड बॉक्स के बारे में सोचें।

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM) is the bigger box — it covers sourcing raw materials, negotiating with suppliers, planning production, forecasting demand, and coordinating everyone from the cotton farmer to the cashier.
segments.tr: आपूर्ति श्रृंखला प्रबंधन (SCM) बड़ा बॉक्स है — यह कच्चे माल की सोर्सिंग, आपूर्तिकर्ताओं के साथ बातचीत, उत्पादन की योजना, मांग पूर्वानुमान, और कपास किसान से लेकर कैशियर तक सभी को समन्वय करता है।

segments.src: Logistics is the box inside it that handles physical flow and storage.
segments.tr: लॉजिस्टिक्स इसके अंदर का बॉक्स है जो भौतिक प्रवाह और भंडारण को संभालता है।

segments.src: A useful shorthand:
segments.tr: एक उपयोगी संक्षिप्त नाम:

segments.src: - **SCM asks:** who should make this, where, in what quantity, and on what terms?
segments.tr: - **SCM पूछता है:** इसे कौन बनाना चाहिए, कहां, किस मात्रा में, और किन शर्तों पर?

segments.src: - **Logistics asks:** given those decisions, how does it physically get there, how fast, and at what cost?
segments.tr: - **लॉजिस्टिक्स पूछता है:** उन निर्णयों को देखते हुए, यह शारीरिक रूप से वहां कैसे पहुंचता है, कितनी तेजी से, और किस लागत पर?

segments.src: You can't do good SCM without logistics, but logistics alone won't save you from a bad sourcing decision.
segments.tr: आप लॉजिस्टिक्स के बिना अच्छा SCM नहीं कर सकते, लेकिन अकेले लॉजिस्टिक्स आपको खराब सोर्सिंग निर्णय से नहीं बचा सकता।

segments.src: If your supplier is 8,000 miles away and your product has a six-week shelf life, no amount of clever routing fixes that.
segments.tr: यदि आपूर्तिकर्ता 8,000 मील दूर है और आपके उत्पाद का शेल्फ जीवन छह सप्ताह है, तो चतुर राउटिंग की कोई भी मात्रा इसे ठीक नहीं करेगी।

segments.src: The other thing to know upfront: logistics is a **trade-off machine**, not an optimization with one answer.
segments.tr: एक और बात जो पहले से जाननी है: लॉजिस्टिक्स एक **ट्रेड-ऑफ मशीन** है, एक अनुकूलन नहीं जिसका एक उत्तर है।

segments.src: Air freight is fast and expensive; ocean is cheap and slow.
segments.tr: हवाई माल तेज़ और महंगा है; समुद्र सस्ता और धीमा है।

segments.src: Holding lots of inventory means you never stock out, but the industry rule of thumb is that carrying inventory costs roughly 20–25% of its value per year in capital, warehousing, insurance, and obsolescence.
segments.tr: बहुत अधिक स्टॉक रखने का मतलब है कि आप कभी स्टॉक खत्म नहीं करते हैं, लेकिन उद्योग का अंगूठे का नियम यह है कि स्टॉक ले जाना लगभग 20–25% इसके मूल्य का प्रति वर्ष पूंजी, गोदाम, बीमा और अप्रचलितता में लागत करता है।

segments.src: Five regional warehouses shorten delivery times but multiply fixed costs.
segments.tr: पाँच क्षेत्रीय गोदाम डिलीवरी समय को कम करते हैं लेकिन निश्चित लागत को गुणा करते हैं।

segments.src: Every logistics decision is somebody choosing a point on a curve — usually the curve between **cost and speed**, or between **cost and reliability**.
segments.tr: हर लॉजिस्टिक्स निर्णय कोई एक वक्र पर एक बिंदु चुनने का है — आमतौर पर **लागत और गति** के बीच का वक्र, या **लागत और विश्वसनीयता** के बीच का वक्र।

segments.src: ## 일상 속에서
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा में

segments.src: You order running shoes for $89 on a Sunday night from your couch in Denver.
segments.tr: आप डेनवर में अपने सोफे से रविवार की रात को $89 के लिए दौड़ने के जूते ऑर्डर करते हैं।

segments.src: Free two-day shipping.
segments.tr: मुफ्त दो दिन की शिपिंग।

segments.src: Here's the invisible machine that runs before Tuesday.
segments.tr: यहाँ अदृश्य मशीन है जो मंगलवार से पहले चलती है।

segments.src: The moment you click, an inventory system decides *which* of several U.S.
segments.tr: जैसे ही आप क्लिक करते हैं, एक इन्वेंटरी सिस्टम यह तय करता है कि कई यू.एस. में से *कौन सा*।

segments.src: fulfillment centers should ship — not necessarily the closest one, but the one that balances distance, stock levels, and how many other Denver-bound orders it can consolidate into the same truck.
segments.tr: पूर्ति केंद्र शिप करना चाहिए — जरूरी नहीं कि सबसे करीबी हो, बल्कि जो दूरी, स्टॉक स्तर और कितने अन्य डेनवर-बाउंड ऑर्डर को एक ही ट्रक में समेकित कर सकता है।

segments.src: A worker (or increasingly, a robotic shelf-mover) picks your box, and it gets sorted onto a line-haul truck.
segments.tr: एक कार्यकर्ता (या तेजी से, एक रोबोटिक शेल्फ-मूवर) आपके बॉक्स को चुनता है, और इसे एक लाइन-हॉल ट्रक पर सॉर्ट किया जाता है।

segments.src: That truck may run to a sorting hub — the two most famous in the country are UPS's Worldport in Louisville, Kentucky, and FedEx's superhub in Memphis, Tennessee, both of which exist because they sit near the population-weighted center of the U.S.
segments.tr: वह ट्रक एक सॉर्टिंग हब तक जा सकता है — देश में दो सबसे प्रसिद्ध UPS का लुइसविल, केंटकी में Worldport और FedEx का मेम्फिस, टेनेसी में superhub हैं, दोनों मौजूद हैं क्योंकि वे यू.एस. के जनसंख्या-भारित केंद्र के पास बैठते हैं।

segments.src: and let packages from everywhere meet, re-sort overnight, and fly back out before dawn.
segments.tr: और सभी जगहों से पैकेज को मिलने दें, रात भर फिर से सॉर्ट करें, और सूर्योदय से पहले वापस उड़ान भरें।

segments.src: From there your box moves to a local delivery station, gets loaded onto a van with 150 other stops, and a route algorithm decides the driver's sequence.
segments.tr: वहां से आपका बॉक्स एक स्थानीय डिलीवरी स्टेशन पर जाता है, 150 अन्य स्टॉप के साथ एक वैन पर लोड किया जाता है, और एक रूट एल्गोरिथम ड्राइवर के अनुक्रम को तय करता है।

segments.src: That final leg — the delivery station to your door — is called the **last mile**, and it's routinely the single most expensive segment of the whole journey.
segments.tr: वह अंतिम पैर — डिलीवरी स्टेशन से आपके दरवाजे तक — को **अंतिम मील** कहा जाता है, और यह आमतौर पर पूरी यात्रा का सबसे महंगा खंड है।

segments.src: One truck crossing Nebraska carries thousands of packages at once; one van in a Denver neighborhood carries a few hundred and burns an hour in traffic.
segments.tr: नेब्रास्का को पार करने वाला एक ट्रक एक बार में हजारों पैकेज ले जाता है; डेनवर के पड़ोस में एक वैन कुछ सौ पैकेज ले जाता है और ट्रैफिक में एक घंटा बर्बाद करता है।

segments.src: Trucking is the largest single line item in U.S.
segments.tr: ट्रकिंग यू.एस. में सबसे बड़ी एकल पंक्ति है।

segments.src: logistics spending, and last-mile delivery is why.
segments.tr: लॉजिस्टिक्स व्यय, और अंतिम-मील डिलीवरी इसका कारण है।

segments.src: "Free shipping" is, of course, not free.
segments.tr: "मुफ्त शिपिंग" निश्चित रूप से मुफ्त नहीं है।

segments.src: It's priced into the $89, subsidized by your membership fee, or absorbed as a customer-acquisition cost.
segments.tr: यह $89 में मूल्य है, आपकी सदस्यता शुल्क द्वारा सब्सिडी प्राप्त है, या ग्राहक-अधिग्रहण लागत के रूप में अवशोषित है।

segments.src: Somebody paid for the van.
segments.tr: किसी ने वैन के लिए भुगतान किया।

segments.src: Now zoom out.
segments.tr: अब बाहर निकलें।

segments.src: Recent CSCMP *State of Logistics* reports put total U.S.
segments.tr: हाल के CSCMP *State of Logistics* रिपोर्ट कुल यू.एस. को रखते हैं।

segments.src: business logistics costs at roughly **$2.5 trillion, or about 8–9% of GDP**.
segments.tr: व्यावसायिक लॉजिस्टिक्स लागत लगभग **$2.5 ट्रिलियन, या लगभग 8–9% GDP** पर।

segments.src: That's the scale of the industry that made your Tuesday delivery unremarkable.
segments.tr: यह उद्योग के पैमाने के बारे में है जिसने आपकी मंगलवार की डिलीवरी को साधारण बना दिया।

segments.src: And it's changing fast.
segments.tr: और यह तेजी से बदल रहा है।

segments.src: Four trends worth knowing:
segments.tr: जानने योग्य चार प्रवृत्तियां:

segments.src: 1. **E-commerce reshaped the network.** Retail logistics used to mean moving pallets to a few hundred stores. Now it means moving single boxes to millions of homes — a completely different cost structure, which is why warehouse space near cities got so valuable.
segments.tr: 1. **ई-कॉमर्स ने नेटवर्क को फिर से आकार दिया।** खुदरा लॉजिस्टिक्स पैलेट को कुछ सौ स्टोरों में ले जाने का मतलब था। अब इसका मतलब एकल बक्सों को लाखों घरों तक ले जाना है — एक पूरी तरह से अलग लागत संरचना, यही कारण है कि शहरों के पास गोदाम स्थान बहुत मूल्यवान हो गया।

segments.src: 2. **Automation is filling warehouses**, driven by both labor shortages and volume — robotic picking, automated sortation, and warehouse management software.
segments.tr: 2. **ऑटोमेशन गोदाम भर रहा है**, श्रम की कमी और मात्रा दोनों द्वारा संचालित — रोबोटिक पिकिंग, स्वचालित सॉर्टेशन, और गोदाम प्रबंधन सॉफ्टवेयर।

segments.src: 3. **Resilience is now a board-level word.** The 2020–2022 disruptions — port congestion, the Suez blockage, chip shortages — taught companies that the cheapest supply chain and the most reliable one are rarely the same. Hence "nearshoring," dual sourcing, and holding a bit more safety stock than pure efficiency would suggest.
segments.tr: 3. **लचीलापन अब एक बोर्ड-स्तर का शब्द है।** 2020–2022 के व्यवधान — बंदरगाह भीड़, स्वेज नाकाबंदी, चिप की कमी — कंपनियों को सिखाया कि सबसे सस्ती आपूर्ति श्रृंखला और सबसे विश्वसनीय आमतौर पर समान नहीं होती है। इसलिए "nearshoring," दोहरी सोर्सिंग, और शुद्ध दक्षता की तुलना में थोड़ा अधिक सुरक्षा स्टॉक रखना।

segments.src: 4. **Visibility is the new battleground.** Knowing exactly where a shipment is, and predicting when it will actually arrive, is often worth more than shaving a few cents off the freight rate.
segments.tr: 4. **दृश्यता नया युद्धक्षेत्र है।** यह जानना कि एक शिपमेंट कहां है, और यह भविष्यवाणी करना कि यह वास्तव में कब पहुंचेगा, अक्सर माल दर से कुछ सेंट शेविंग करने से कहीं अधिक मूल्यवान होता है।

segments.src: A last practical concept: when comparing two suppliers, the sticker price is the wrong number.
segments.tr: एक अंतिम व्यावहारिक अवधारणा: दो आपूर्तिकर्ताओं की तुलना करते समय, स्टिकर मूल्य गलत संख्या है।

segments.src: What matters is **landed cost**:
segments.tr: जो मायने रखता है वह है **लैंडेड लागत**:

segments.src: Landed cost = unit price + freight + duties/tariffs + insurance + handling
segments.tr: Landed cost = unit price + freight + duties/tariffs + insurance + handling

segments.src: - **Landed cost** — The all-in cost of getting a purchased item to your door: unit price plus freight, duties, insurance, and handling.

es.title: [Logística 101 #1] El Trabajo de Billones de Dólares que Nadie Ve: Qué es Realmente la Logística

segments.src: > Logistics is the work of getting the right thing to the right place at the right time and cost — and in the U.S. it's roughly a $2.5 trillion-a-year industry that most people only notice when it fails.
segments.tr: > La logística es el trabajo de poner la cosa correcta en el lugar correcto al momento correcto y costo correcto — y en EE.UU. es aproximadamente una industria de $2.5 billones anuales que la mayoría de la gente solo nota cuando falla.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## Concepto de hoy

segments.src: Ask someone what logistics is and you'll usually hear "trucks."
segments.tr: Si le preguntas a alguien qué es la logística, generalmente escucharás "camiones".

segments.src: That's like saying finance is "ATMs."
segments.tr: Es como decir que las finanzas son "cajeros automáticos".

segments.src: The trade association CSCMP defines logistics management as the part of supply chain management that plans, implements, and controls the efficient flow and storage of goods, services, and related information — from the point of origin to the point of consumption, and back again.
segments.tr: La asociación comercial CSCMP define la gestión logística como la parte de la gestión de la cadena de suministro que planifica, implementa y controla el flujo y almacenamiento eficiente de bienes, servicios e información relacionada — desde el punto de origen hasta el punto de consumo, y de regreso.

segments.src: Strip out the jargon and you get four verbs: **move, store, handle, inform.**
segments.tr: Elimina la jerga y obtienes cuatro verbos: **mover, almacenar, manipular, informar.**

segments.src: Practitioners often summarize the goal as the **seven rights**: the right product, in the right quantity, in the right condition, at the right place, at the right time, to the right customer, at the right cost.
segments.tr: Los profesionales a menudo resumen el objetivo como los **siete derechos**: el producto correcto, en la cantidad correcta, en la condición correcta, en el lugar correcto, en el momento correcto, para el cliente correcto, al costo correcto.

segments.src: Notice that six of the seven are about *service* and only one is about *price*.
segments.tr: Observa que seis de los siete son acerca del *servicio* y solo uno es acerca del *precio*.

segments.src: That tension is the entire discipline.
segments.tr: Esa tensión es toda la disciplina.

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: logistics doesn't change what a product *is*.
segments.tr: Aquí está la parte que sorprende a la gente: la logística no cambia lo que un producto *es*.

segments.src: A pair of running shoes sitting in a warehouse in Ohio is chemically identical to the same pair on your doorstep in Denver.
segments.tr: Un par de zapatos para correr en un almacén en Ohio es químicamente idéntico al mismo par en tu puerta en Denver.

segments.src: What logistics creates is **place utility** (value from being where you need it) and **time utility** (value from being there when you need it).
segments.tr: Lo que la logística crea es **utilidad de lugar** (valor por estar donde lo necesitas) y **utilidad de tiempo** (valor por estar allí cuando lo necesitas).

segments.src: An umbrella in a warehouse is inventory.
segments.tr: Un paraguas en un almacén es inventario.

segments.src: An umbrella in a store lobby during a downpour is a sale.
segments.tr: Un paraguas en una tienda durante una lluvia torrencial es una venta.

segments.src: **So how is this different from supply chain management?** Think of nested boxes.
segments.tr: **¿Entonces cómo es esto diferente de la gestión de la cadena de suministro?** Piensa en cajas anidadas.

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM) is the bigger box — it covers sourcing raw materials, negotiating with suppliers, planning production, forecasting demand, and coordinating everyone from the cotton farmer to the cashier.
segments.tr: La gestión de la cadena de suministro (SCM) es la caja más grande — cubre el abastecimiento de materias primas, negociación con proveedores, planificación de producción, pronóstico de demanda, y coordinación de todos, desde el cultivador de algodón hasta el cajero.

segments.src: Logistics is the box inside it that handles physical flow and storage.
segments.tr: La logística es la caja dentro de ella que maneja el flujo físico y el almacenamiento.

segments.src: A useful shorthand:
segments.tr: Una abreviatura útil:

segments.src: - **SCM asks:** who should make this, where, in what quantity, and on what terms?
segments.tr: - **SCM pregunta:** ¿quién debería hacer esto, dónde, en qué cantidad y en qué términos?

segments.src: - **Logistics asks:** given those decisions, how does it physically get there, how fast, and at what cost?
segments.tr: - **La logística pregunta:** dados esas decisiones, ¿cómo llega físicamente, qué tan rápido y a qué costo?

segments.src: You can't do good SCM without logistics, but logistics alone won't save you from a bad sourcing decision.
segments.tr: No puedes hacer una buena SCM sin logística, pero la logística sola no te salvará de una mala decisión de abastecimiento.

segments.src: If your supplier is 8,000 miles away and your product has a six-week shelf life, no amount of clever routing fixes that.
segments.tr: Si tu proveedor está a 8,000 millas de distancia y tu producto tiene una vida útil de seis semanas, ninguna cantidad de enrutamiento inteligente lo soluciona.

segments.src: The other thing to know upfront: logistics is a **trade-off machine**, not an optimization with one answer.
segments.tr: Otra cosa que debes saber de antemano: la logística es una **máquina de compensaciones**, no una optimización con una sola respuesta.

segments.src: Air freight is fast and expensive; ocean is cheap and slow.
segments.tr: El flete aéreo es rápido y caro; el marítimo es barato y lento.

segments.src: Holding lots of inventory means you never stock out, but the industry rule of thumb is that carrying inventory costs roughly 20–25% of its value per year in capital, warehousing, insurance, and obsolescence.
segments.tr: Mantener mucho inventario significa que nunca se te acaba el stock, pero la regla general de la industria es que el costo de llevar inventario es aproximadamente 20–25% de su valor por año en capital, almacenamiento, seguros y obsolescencia.

segments.src: Five regional warehouses shorten delivery times but multiply fixed costs.
segments.tr: Cinco almacenes regionales acortan los tiempos de entrega pero multiplican los costos fijos.

segments.src: Every logistics decision is somebody choosing a point on a curve — usually the curve between **cost and speed**, or between **cost and reliability**.
segments.tr: Cada decisión logística es alguien eligiendo un punto en una curva — generalmente la curva entre **costo y velocidad**, o entre **costo y confiabilidad**.

segments.tr: en aproximadamente **$2.5 billones, o alrededor del 8–9% del PIB**.

segments.src: That's the scale of the industry that made your Tuesday delivery unremarkable.
segments.tr: Esa es la escala de la industria que hizo que tu entrega del martes fuera algo común.

segments.src: And it's changing fast.
segments.tr: Y está cambiando rápidamente.

segments.src: Four trends worth knowing:
segments.tr: Cuatro tendencias que vale la pena conocer:

segments.src: 1. **E-commerce reshaped the network.** Retail logistics used to mean moving pallets to a few hundred stores. Now it means moving single boxes to millions of homes — a completely different cost structure, which is why warehouse space near cities got so valuable.
segments.tr: 1. **El comercio electrónico remodeló la red.** La logística minorista solía significar mover paletas a unos pocos cientos de tiendas. Ahora significa mover cajas individuales a millones de hogares — una estructura de costos completamente diferente, por lo que el espacio de almacén cerca de las ciudades se volvió muy valioso.

segments.src: 2. **Automation is filling warehouses**, driven by both labor shortages and volume — robotic picking, automated sortation, and warehouse management software.
segments.tr: 2. **La automatización está llenando almacenes**, impulsada tanto por la escasez de mano de obra como por el volumen — recogida robótica, clasificación automatizada y software de gestión de almacenes.

segments.src: 3. **Resilience is now a board-level word.** The 2020–2022 disruptions — port congestion, the Suez blockage, chip shortages — taught companies that the cheapest supply chain and the most reliable one are rarely the same. Hence "nearshoring," dual sourcing, and holding a bit more safety stock than pure efficiency would suggest.
segments.tr: 3. **La resiliencia es ahora una palabra de nivel de junta directiva.** Las disrupciones de 2020–2022 — congestión portuaria, el bloqueo de Suez, escasez de chips — enseñaron a las empresas que la cadena de suministro más barata y la más confiable rara vez son iguales. Por lo tanto, "nearshoring", abastecimiento dual, y mantener un poco más de stock de seguridad del que la eficiencia pura sugeriría.

segments.src: 4. **Visibility is the new battleground.** Knowing exactly where a shipment is, and predicting when it will actually arrive, is often worth more than shaving a few cents off the freight rate.
segments.tr: 4. **La visibilidad es el nuevo campo de batalla.** Saber exactamente dónde está un envío, y predecir cuándo realmente llegará, a menudo vale más que ahorrar unos pocos centavos de la tarifa de flete.

segments.src: A last practical concept: when comparing two suppliers, the sticker price is the wrong number.
segments.tr: Un concepto práctico final: cuando se comparan dos proveedores, el precio de etiqueta es el número incorrecto.

segments.tr: ## Resumen de 3 líneas

segments.src: 1. Logistics is the move-store-handle-inform work that creates **place and time utility** — it doesn't change the product, it changes where and when it's available.
segments.tr: 1. La logística es el trabajo de mover-almacenar-manipular-informar que crea **utilidad de lugar y tiempo** — no cambia el producto, cambia dónde y cuándo está disponible.

segments.src: 2. Logistics is a **subset of supply chain management**: SCM decides who makes what, where, and how much; logistics executes the physical flow and storage.
segments.tr: 2. La logística es un **subconjunto de la gestión de la cadena de suministro**: SCM decide quién hace qué, dónde y cuánto; la logística ejecuta el flujo físico y el almacenamiento.

segments.src: 3. Every logistics decision is a **trade-off** among cost, speed, and reliability — and the honest number to compare is landed cost, not sticker price.
segments.tr: 3. Cada decisión logística es una **compensación** entre costo, velocidad y confiabilidad — y el número honesto a comparar es el costo de llegada, no el precio de etiqueta.

segments.src: - **Logistics** — Planning and controlling the efficient flow and storage of goods, services, and related information from origin to consumption, including returns.
segments.tr: - **Logística** — Planificación y control del flujo y almacenamiento eficiente de bienes, servicios e información relacionada desde el origen hasta el consumo, incluyendo devoluciones.

segments.src: - **Supply Chain Management (SCM)** — The broader coordination of sourcing, production, planning, and distribution across all partners from raw material to end customer; logistics sits inside it.
segments.tr: - **Gestión de la Cadena de Suministro (SCM)** — La coordinación más amplia del abastecimiento, producción, planificación y distribución en todos los socios, desde la materia prima hasta el cliente final; la logística se encuentra dentro de ella.

segments.src: - **Last mile** — The final delivery leg from a local facility to the customer's door; typically the most expensive segment per package.
segments.tr: - **Última milla** — El tramo de entrega final desde una instalación local hasta la puerta del cliente; típicamente el segmento más caro por paquete.

segments.src: - **Lead time** — Total elapsed time from placing an order to receiving it; the number customers actually feel.
segments.tr: - **Tiempo de entrega** — Tiempo total transcurrido desde hacer un pedido hasta recibirlo; el número que los clientes realmente sienten.

segments.src: - **Landed cost** — The all-in cost of getting a purchased item to your door: unit price plus freight, duties, insurance, and handling.
segments.tr: - **Costo de llegada** — El costo total de llevar un artículo comprado a tu puerta: precio unitario más flete, aranceles, seguros y manipulación.

segments.src: - **3PL (third-party logistics)** — An outside company hired to run warehousing, transportation, or fulfillment on your behalf instead of doing it in-house.
segments.tr: - **3PL (logística de terceros)** — Una empresa externa contratada para ejecutar almacenamiento, transporte o cumplimiento en tu nombre en lugar de hacerlo internamente.

segments.src: Long-haul legs spread their cost across thousands of packages; a delivery van covers far fewer stops per hour, so the last mile carries a disproportionate share of total delivery cost.
segments.tr: Los tramos de larga distancia distribuyen su costo entre miles de paquetes; una furgoneta de entrega hace muchas menos paradas por hora, por lo que la última milla lleva una parte desproporcionada del costo total de entrega.

segments.src: > Logistics is the work of getting the right thing to the right place at the right time and cost — and in the U.S. it's roughly a $2.5 trillion-a-year industry that most people only notice when it fails.
segments.tr: > اللوجستيات هي عملية إيصال الشيء الصحيح إلى المكان الصحيح في الوقت الصحيح وبالتكلفة الصحيحة — وفي الولايات المتحدة، تعتبر صناعة بقيمة حوالي 2.5 تريليون دولار سنوياً، يلاحظها معظم الناس فقط عندما تفشل.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## المفهوم اليوم

segments.src: Ask someone what logistics is and you'll usually hear "trucks."
segments.tr: اطلب من شخص ما أن يخبرك ما هي اللوجستيات وستسمع عادة "الشاحنات".

segments.src: That's like saying finance is "ATMs."
segments.tr: هذا مثل القول بأن التمويل هو "أجهزة الصراف الآلي".

segments.src: The trade association CSCMP defines logistics management as the part of supply chain management that plans, implements, and controls the efficient flow and storage of goods, services, and related information — from the point of origin to the point of consumption, and back again.
segments.tr: تعرّف جمعية التجارة CSCMP إدارة اللوجستيات بأنها جزء من إدارة سلسلة التوريد الذي يخطط وينفذ ويتحكم في التدفق الفعال والتخزين للسلع والخدمات والمعلومات ذات الصلة — من نقطة الأصل إلى نقطة الاستهلاك، والعودة مرة أخرى.

segments.src: Strip out the jargon and you get four verbs: **move, store, handle, inform.**
segments.tr: إذا أزلنا المصطلحات الفنية، ستحصل على أربعة أفعال: **النقل والتخزين والمناولة والإعلام**.

segments.src: Practitioners often summarize the goal as the **seven rights**: the right product, in the right quantity, in the right condition, at the right place, at the right time, to the right customer, at the right cost.
segments.tr: يختصر الممارسون الهدف غالباً في **الحقوق السبعة**: المنتج الصحيح، بالكمية الصحيحة، في الحالة الصحيحة، في المكان الصحيح، في الوقت الصحيح، للعميل الصحيح، بالسعر الصحيح.

segments.src: Notice that six of the seven are about *service* and only one is about *price*.
segments.tr: لاحظ أن ستة من السبعة تتعلق بـ *الخدمة* وواحد فقط يتعلق بـ *السعر*.

segments.src: That tension is the entire discipline.
segments.tr: هذا التوتر هو التخصص كله.

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: logistics doesn't change what a product *is*.
segments.tr: إليك الجزء الذي يفاجئ الناس: اللوجستيات لا تغير ما *هو* المنتج.

segments.src: A pair of running shoes sitting in a warehouse in Ohio is chemically identical to the same pair on your doorstep in Denver.
segments.tr: زوج من أحذية الركض الموجودة في مستودع في أوهايو متطابق كيميائياً مع نفس الزوج على باب منزلك في دنفر.

segments.src: What logistics creates is **place utility** (value from being where you need it) and **time utility** (value from being there when you need it).
segments.tr: ما تنشئه اللوجستيات هو **المنفعة المكانية** (قيمة الوجود حيث تحتاجها) و **منفعة الوقت** (قيمة الوجود عندما تحتاجها).

segments.src: An umbrella in a warehouse is inventory.
segments.tr: المظلة في مستودع هي مخزون.

segments.src: An umbrella in a store lobby during a downpour is a sale.
segments.tr: المظلة في ردهة متجر أثناء هطول الأمطار الغزيرة هي عملية بيع.

segments.src: **So how is this different from supply chain management?** Think of nested boxes.
segments.tr: **إذن، كيف يختلف هذا عن إدارة سلسلة التوريد؟** فكر في صناديق متداخلة.

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM) is the bigger box — it covers sourcing raw materials, negotiating with suppliers, planning production, forecasting demand, and coordinating everyone from the cotton farmer to the cashier.
segments.tr: إدارة سلسلة التوريد (SCM) هي الصندوق الأكبر — فهي تغطي الحصول على المواد الخام والتفاوض مع الموردين وتخطيط الإنتاج والتنبؤ بالطلب وتنسيق الجميع من المزارع القطن إلى صراف المتجر.

segments.src: Logistics is the box inside it that handles physical flow and storage.
segments.tr: اللوجستيات هي الصندوق الموجود بداخلها الذي يتعامل مع التدفق المادي والتخزين.

segments.src: A useful shorthand:
segments.tr: اختصار مفيد:

segments.src: - **SCM asks:** who should make this, where, in what quantity, and on what terms?
segments.tr: - **إدارة سلسلة التوريد تسأل:** من الذي يجب أن يصنع هذا، وأين، وبأي كمية، وعلى أي شروط؟

segments.src: - **Logistics asks:** given those decisions, how does it physically get there, how fast, and at what cost?
segments.tr: - **اللوجستيات تسأل:** نظراً لهذه القرارات، كيف يصل فعلياً هناك، وبأي سرعة، وبأي تكلفة؟

segments.src: You can't do good SCM without logistics, but logistics alone won't save you from a bad sourcing decision.
segments.tr: لا يمكنك القيام بإدارة سلسلة توريد جيدة بدون لوجستيات، لكن اللوجستيات وحدها لن تنقذك من قرار توريد سيء.

segments.src: If your supplier is 8,000 miles away and your product has a six-week shelf life, no amount of clever routing fixes that.
segments.tr: إذا كان المورد لديك على بعد 8000 ميل وكان منتجك يتمتع بفترة صلاحية مدتها ستة أسابيع، فلا توجد كمية من التوجيه الذكي تصلح ذلك.

segments.src: The other thing to know upfront: logistics is a **trade-off machine**, not an optimization with one answer.
segments.tr: الشيء الآخر الذي يجب معرفته مسبقاً: اللوجستيات هي **آلة المقايضة**، وليست تحسيناً بإجابة واحدة.

segments.src: Air freight is fast and expensive; ocean is cheap and slow.
segments.tr: النقل الجوي سريع وباهظ الثمن؛ والنقل البحري رخيص وبطيء.

segments.src: Holding lots of inventory means you never stock out, but the industry rule of thumb is that carrying inventory costs roughly 20–25% of its value per year in capital, warehousing, insurance, and obsolescence.
segments.tr: الاحتفاظ بكميات كبيرة من المخزون يعني أنك لن تنفد أبداً، لكن القاعدة الشائعة في الصناعة هي أن تكاليف حمل المخزون تبلغ تقريباً 20-25% من قيمته سنوياً في رأس المال والتخزين والتأمين والتقادم.

segments.src: Five regional warehouses shorten delivery times but multiply fixed costs.
segments.tr: خمسة مستودعات إقليمية تقصر أوقات التسليم لكنها تضاعف التكاليف الثابتة.

segments.src: Every logistics decision is somebody choosing a point on a curve — usually the curve between **cost and speed**, or between **cost and reliability**.
segments.tr: كل قرار لوجستي هو شخص ما يختار نقطة على منحنى — عادة المنحنى بين **التكلفة والسرعة**، أو بين **التكلفة والموثوقية**.

fr.title: [Logistics 101 #1] Le Travail de Mille Milliards de Dollars Que Personne ne Voit : Ce Qu'est Vraiment la Logistique

segments.src: > Logistics is the work of getting the right thing to the right place at the right time and cost — and in the U.S. it's roughly a $2.5 trillion-a-year industry that most people only notice when it fails.
segments.tr: > La logistique est le travail qui consiste à amener la bonne chose au bon endroit au bon moment et au bon coût — et aux États-Unis, c'est une industrie d'environ 2,5 trillions de dollars par an que la plupart des gens ne remarquent que lorsqu'elle échoue.

segments.src: ## 오늘의 개념
segments.tr: ## Concept du jour

segments.src: Ask someone what logistics is and you'll usually hear "trucks."
segments.tr: Demandez à quelqu'un ce qu'est la logistique et vous entendrez généralement « des camions ».

segments.src: That's like saying finance is "ATMs."
segments.tr: C'est comme dire que la finance est « des guichets automatiques ».

segments.src: The trade association CSCMP defines logistics management as the part of supply chain management that plans, implements, and controls the efficient flow and storage of goods, services, and related information — from the point of origin to the point of consumption, and back again.
segments.tr: L'association commerciale CSCMP définit la gestion logistique comme la partie de la gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement qui planifie, met en œuvre et contrôle le flux efficace et le stockage des marchandises, services et informations connexes — du point d'origine au point de consommation, et retour.

segments.src: Strip out the jargon and you get four verbs: **move, store, handle, inform.**
segments.tr: Supprimez le jargon et vous obtenez quatre verbes : **déplacer, stocker, manipuler, informer.**

segments.src: Practitioners often summarize the goal as the **seven rights**: the right product, in the right quantity, in the right condition, at the right place, at the right time, to the right customer, at the right cost.
segments.tr: Les praticiens résument souvent l'objectif par les **sept droits** : le bon produit, en bonne quantité, en bon état, au bon endroit, au bon moment, au bon client, au bon coût.

segments.src: Notice that six of the seven are about *service* and only one is about *price*.
segments.tr: Remarquez que six des sept concernent le *service* et un seul concerne le *prix*.

segments.src: That tension is the entire discipline.
segments.tr: Cette tension est toute la discipline.

segments.src: Here's the part that surprises people: logistics doesn't change what a product *is*.
segments.tr: Voici la partie qui surprend les gens : la logistique ne change pas ce qu'un produit *est*.

segments.src: A pair of running shoes sitting in a warehouse in Ohio is chemically identical to the same pair on your doorstep in Denver.
segments.tr: Une paire de chaussures de course assise dans un entrepôt en Ohio est chimiquement identique à la même paire sur votre pas de porte à Denver.

segments.src: What logistics creates is **place utility** (value from being where you need it) and **time utility** (value from being there when you need it).
segments.tr: Ce que la logistique crée, c'est l'**utilité de lieu** (valeur du fait d'être où vous en avez besoin) et l'**utilité de temps** (valeur du fait d'y être quand vous en avez besoin).

segments.src: An umbrella in a warehouse is inventory.
segments.tr: Un parapluie dans un entrepôt est un inventaire.

segments.src: An umbrella in a store lobby during a downpour is a sale.
segments.tr: Un parapluie dans le hall d'un magasin pendant une averse est une vente.

segments.src: **So how is this different from supply chain management?** Think of nested boxes.
segments.tr: **Alors, en quoi cela diffère-t-il de la gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement ?** Pensez à des boîtes imbriquées.

segments.src: Supply chain management (SCM) is the bigger box — it covers sourcing raw materials, negotiating with suppliers, planning production, forecasting demand, and coordinating everyone from the cotton farmer to the cashier.
segments.tr: La gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement (SCM) est la plus grande boîte — elle couvre l'approvisionnement en matières premières, la négociation avec les fournisseurs, la planification de la production, la prévision de la demande et la coordination de tous, du producteur de coton au caissier.

segments.src: Logistics is the box inside it that handles physical flow and storage.
segments.tr: La logistique est la boîte intérieure qui gère le flux physique et le stockage.

segments.src: A useful shorthand:
segments.tr: Un raccourci utile :

segments.src: - **SCM asks:** who should make this, where, in what quantity, and on what terms?
segments.tr: - **SCM demande :** qui devrait faire cela, où, en quelle quantité, et à quelles conditions ?

segments.src: - **Logistics asks:** given those decisions, how does it physically get there, how fast, and at what cost?
segments.tr: - **La logistique demande :** étant donné ces décisions, comment cela y arrive-t-il physiquement, à quelle vitesse et à quel coût ?

segments.src: You can't do good SCM without logistics, but logistics alone won't save you from a bad sourcing decision.
segments.tr: Vous ne pouvez pas faire une bonne SCM sans logistique, mais la logistique seule ne vous sauvera pas d'une mauvaise décision d'approvisionnement.

segments.src: If your supplier is 8,000 miles away and your product has a six-week shelf life, no amount of clever routing fixes that.
segments.tr: Si votre fournisseur est à 8 000 miles de distance et que votre produit a une durée de conservation de six semaines, aucun routage intelligent ne peut corriger cela.

segments.src: The other thing to know upfront: logistics is a **trade-off machine**, not an optimization with one answer.
segments.tr: L'autre chose à savoir d'avance : la logistique est une **machine de compromis**, pas une optimisation avec une seule réponse.

segments.src: Air freight is fast and expensive; ocean is cheap and slow.
segments.tr: Le fret aérien est rapide et coûteux ; le transport maritime est bon marché et lent.

segments.src: Holding lots of inventory means you never stock out, but the industry rule of thumb is that carrying inventory costs roughly 20–25% of its value per year in capital, warehousing, insurance, and obsolescence.
segments.tr: Tenir beaucoup d'inventaire signifie que vous ne manquez jamais de stock, mais la règle d'or de l'industrie est que la gestion des stocks coûte environ 20–25 % de sa valeur par an en capital, entreposage, assurance et obsolescence.

segments.src: Five regional warehouses shorten delivery times but multiply fixed costs.
segments.tr: Cinq entrepôts régionaux raccourcissent les délais de livraison mais multiplient les coûts fixes.

segments.src: Every logistics decision is somebody choosing a point on a curve — usually the curve between **cost and speed**, or between **cost and reliability**.
segments.tr: Chaque décision logistique est quelqu'un qui choisit un point sur une courbe — généralement la courbe entre **coût et vitesse**, ou entre **coût et fiabilité**.

segments.tr: ## Dans la vie quotidienne

segments.src: You order running shoes for $89 on a Sunday night from your couch in Denver.

segments.src: A worker (or increasingly, a robotic shelf-mover) picks your box, and it gets sorted onto a line-haul truck.
segments.tr: Un travailleur (ou de plus en plus, un engin de déplacement de rayons robotisé) prend votre boîte, et elle est triée sur un camion de transport principal.

segments.src: That truck may run to a sorting hub — the two most famous in the country are UPS's Worldport in Louisville, Kentucky, and FedEx's superhub in Memphis, Tennessee, both of which exist because they sit near the population-weighted center of the U.S.
segments.tr: Ce camion peut se diriger vers un centre de tri — les deux plus célèbres du pays sont le Worldport d'UPS à Louisville, Kentucky, et le superhub de FedEx à Memphis, Tennessee, qui existent tous deux parce qu'ils sont situés près du centre pondéré par la population des États-Unis.

segments.src: From there your box moves to a local delivery station, gets loaded onto a van with 150 other stops, and a route algorithm decides the driver's sequence.
segments.tr: De là, votre boîte se déplace vers une station de livraison locale, est chargée sur un camion avec 150 autres arrêts, et un algorithme de routage décide de la séquence du conducteur.

segments.src: That final leg — the delivery station to your door — is called the **last mile**, and it's routinely the single most expensive segment of the whole journey.
segments.tr: Ce dernier tronçon — de la station de livraison à votre porte — s'appelle le **dernier kilomètre**, et c'est régulièrement le segment unique le plus coûteux de tout le voyage.

segments.src: One truck crossing Nebraska carries thousands of packages at once; one van in a Denver neighborhood carries a few hundred and burns an hour in traffic.
segments.tr: Un camion traversant le Nebraska porte des milliers de colis à la fois ; un camion dans un quartier de Denver porte quelques centaines et brûle une heure dans le trafic.

segments.src: Trucking is the largest single line item in U.S.
segments.tr: Le camionnage est le plus grand poste simple dans le budget des États-Unis.

segments.tr: Elle est intégrée aux $89, subventionnée par vos frais d'adhésion ou absorbée en tant que coût d'acquisition de client.

segments.src: Recent CSCMP *State of Logistics* reports put total U.S.
segments.tr: Les récents rapports CSCMP *État de la logistique* placent le total des États-Unis.

segments.src: business logistics costs at roughly **$2.5 trillion, or about 8–9% of GDP**.
segments.tr: coûts de logistique commerciale à environ **2,5 trillions de dollars, ou environ 8–9 % du PIB**.

segments.src: That's the scale of the industry that made your Tuesday delivery unremarkable.
segments.tr: C'est l'échelle de l'industrie qui a rendu votre livraison mardi banale.

segments.src: And it's changing fast.
segments.tr: Et cela change rapidement.

segments.src: Four trends worth knowing:
segments.tr: Quatre tendances à connaître :

segments.src: 1. **E-commerce reshaped the network.** Retail logistics used to mean moving pallets to a few hundred stores. Now it means moving single boxes to millions of homes — a completely different cost structure, which is why warehouse space near cities got so valuable.
segments.tr: 1. **Le commerce électronique a reconfiguré le réseau.** La logistique de vente au détail signifiait autrefois déplacer des palettes vers quelques centaines de magasins. Maintenant, cela signifie déplacer des boîtes uniques vers des millions de maisons — une structure de coûts complètement différente, c'est pourquoi l'espace d'entrepôt près des villes est devenu si précieux.

segments.src: 2. **Automation is filling warehouses**, driven by both labor shortages and volume — robotic picking, automated sortation, and warehouse management software.
segments.tr: 2. **L'automatisation remplit les entrepôts**, entraînée à la fois par les pénuries de main-d'œuvre et le volume — picking robotisé, tri automatisé et logiciels de gestion d'entrepôt.

segments.src: 3. **Resilience is now a board-level word.** The 2020–2022 disruptions — port congestion, the Suez blockage, chip shortages — taught companies that the cheapest supply chain and the most reliable one are rarely the same. Hence "nearshoring," dual sourcing, and holding a bit more safety stock than pure efficiency would suggest.
segments.tr: 3. **La résilience est maintenant un mot au niveau du conseil.** Les perturbations de 2020–2022 — congestion portuaire, le blocage de Suez, les pénuries de puces — ont appris aux entreprises que la chaîne d'approvisionnement la moins chère et la plus fiable sont rarement les mêmes. D'où « le nearshoring », la double source et la détention d'un peu plus de stock de sécurité que l'efficacité pure le suggère.

segments.src: 4. **Visibility is the new battleground.** Knowing exactly where a shipment is, and predicting when it will actually arrive, is often worth more than shaving a few cents off the freight rate.
segments.tr: 4. **La visibilité est le nouveau champ de bataille.** Savoir exactement où se trouve un envoi et prédire quand il arrivera réellement vaut souvent plus que de réduire quelques centimes sur le tarif de fret.

segments.src: A last practical concept: when comparing two suppliers, the sticker price is the wrong number.
segments.tr: Un dernier concept pratique : lors de la comparaison de deux fournisseurs, le prix affiché est le mauvais chiffre.

segments.src: What matters is **landed cost**:
segments.tr: Ce qui compte, c'est le **coût rendu** :

segments.src: Landed cost = unit price + freight + duties/tariffs + insurance + handling
segments.tr: Landed cost = unit price + freight + duties/tariffs + insurance + handling

segments.src: A part that's 15% cheaper from overseas can easily be more expensive once it lands.
segments.tr: Une pièce qui est 15 % moins chère de l'étranger peut facilement être plus chère une fois qu'elle arrive.

segments.src: That single line is why logistics belongs in strategy meetings and not just in the loading dock.
segments.tr: Cette seule ligne est pourquoi la logistique appartient aux réunions stratégiques et non seulement au quai de chargement.

segments.tr: ## Résumé en 3 lignes

segments.src: 1. Logistics is the move-store-handle-inform work that creates **place and time utility** — it doesn't change the product, it changes where and when it's available.
segments.tr: 1. La logistique est le travail de déplacement, stockage, manipulation et information qui crée l'**utilité de lieu et de temps** — cela ne change pas le produit, cela change où et quand il est disponible.

segments.src: 2. Logistics is a **subset of supply chain management**: SCM decides who makes what, where, and how much; logistics executes the physical flow and storage.
segments.tr: 2. La logistique est un **sous-ensemble de la gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement** : la SCM décide qui fabrique quoi, où et combien ; la logistique exécute le flux physique et le stockage.

segments.src: 3. Every logistics decision is a **trade-off** among cost, speed, and reliability — and the honest number to compare is landed cost, not sticker price.
segments.tr: 3. Chaque décision logistique est un **compromis** entre le coût, la vitesse et la fiabilité — et le chiffre honnête à comparer est le coût rendu, pas le prix affiché.

segments.tr: - **Logistique** — Planification et contrôle du flux efficace et du stockage des marchandises, services et informations connexes de l'origine à la consommation, y compris les retours.

segments.src: - **Supply Chain Management (SCM)** — The broader coordination of sourcing, production, planning, and distribution across all partners from raw material to end customer; logistics sits inside it.
segments.tr: - **Gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement (SCM)** — La coordination plus large de l'approvisionnement, la production, la planification et la distribution entre tous les partenaires de la matière première au client final ; la logistique s'inscrit à l'intérieur.

segments.src: - **Last mile** — The final delivery leg from a local facility to the customer's door; typically the most expensive segment per package.
segments.tr: - **Dernier kilomètre** — Le tronçon de livraison final d'une installation locale à la porte du client ; généralement le segment le plus coûteux par colis.

segments.src: - **Lead time** — Total elapsed time from placing an order to receiving it; the number customers actually feel.
segments.tr: - **Délai de livraison** — Temps écoulé total entre la passation d'une commande et sa réception ; le chiffre que les clients ressentent réellement.

segments.src: - **Landed cost** — The all-in cost of getting a purchased item to your door: unit price plus freight, duties, insurance, and handling.
segments.tr: - **Coût rendu** — Le coût all-in pour faire livrer un article acheté à votre porte : prix unitaire plus fret, droits, assurance et manutention.

segments.src: - **3PL (third-party logistics)** — An outside company hired to run warehousing, transportation, or fulfillment on your behalf instead of doing it in-house.
segments.tr: - **3PL (logistique tierce)** — Une entreprise externe engagée pour gérer l'entreposage, le transport ou le traitement des commandes en votre nom au lieu de le faire en interne.

segments.src: Logistics is the physical-flow-and-storage piece nested inside the wider SCM function, which also covers sourcing, demand planning, and supplier strategy.
segments.tr: La logistique est la pièce de flux physique et de stockage imbriquée dans la fonction SCM plus large, qui couvre également l'approvisionnement, la planification de la demande et la stratégie des fournisseurs.

segments.src: Long-haul legs spread their cost across thousands of packages; a delivery van covers far fewer stops per hour, so the last mile carries a disproportionate share of total delivery cost.
segments.tr: Les tronçons longue distance répartissent leur coût sur des milliers de colis ; un camion de livraison couvre bien moins d'arrêts par heure, donc le dernier kilomètre porte une part disproportionnée du coût total de livraison.
